title: Grizzly Feeder
model_title: Vibrating Grizzly Feeder (Feeder Pan + Grizzly Bar Section)

introduction.definition: A vibrating grizzly feeder is a vibrating feeder with a section of parallel bars (the grizzly) at its discharge end. As the material is fed forward, the fines fall through the gaps between the bars and bypass the crusher, while the oversize continues to the crusher. This scalps the feed and reduces crusher load and wear.
applications: Primary crusher feed in quarries and mines
Removing soil and fines before crushing
key_points: Feeds and scalps in one machine
Bar gap sets the scalping size
Bars usually tapered to stop pegging
Fines bypass to save crusher capacity
introduction.summary: A vibrating grizzly feeder combines a feeder pan with a section of tapered grizzly bars. As material vibrates forward, fines fall through the gaps between bars and bypass the crusher; oversize continues to the crusher. This reduces crusher load and wear.

foundation: Support on steelwork or a concrete plinth designed for the hopper/bin load on the feeder plus impact and dynamic loads.
Isolate vibrating machines from the structure with their springs/rubber mounts — never weld or rigidly bolt the vibrating body to the structure.
alignment: Set the feeder at the designed slope and centre it under the hopper outlet; set skirt boards and the hopper gate to the design bed depth.
Align drive and driven shafts (laser or dial gauge) or set the exciter motors as the maker specifies.
piping: Chutes and skirts: allow a gap that widens in the direction of travel so material does not jam; fit dust seals and connect dust extraction where required.
Leave clear access for liner change and for the hopper shut-off gate.
commissioning: Run empty first: check direction, amplitude/speed, temperatures and noise.
Load gradually, check the material bed is even and the discharge rate matches the set-point; record motor current as a baseline.

routine.task: Check for pegged or blocked bar gaps.

periodic.task: Measure bar wear and gap; inspect springs.

overhaul.task: Replace grizzly bars and pan liners.

lubrication: Bearings: grease or oil to the maker's schedule and quantity — do not over-grease vibrating-machine bearings (heat).

symptoms: Feed rate drops, material builds up
remedies: Clean liners; check eccentric weights and spring condition

causes: Fatigue from long running at high amplitude
remedies: Repair to maker's procedure; check amplitude and isolators

safety: Never stand on or clear the grizzly while running; lock out and secure the hopper load.

video_tutorials.title: Grizzly Feeder — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Grizzly Feeder.
A vibrating grizzly feeder is a vibrating feeder with a section of parallel bars (the grizzly) at its discharge end.
As the material is fed forward, the fines fall through the gaps between the bars and bypass the crusher, while the oversize continues to the crusher.
This scalps the feed and reduces crusher load and wear.
Typical applications include primary crusher feed in quarries and mines; scalping of run-of-mine material; removing soil and fines before crushing.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.

script.narration: How the Grizzly Feeder works.
Material from the hopper is fed onto the vibrating pan.
The exciters move the material forward onto the grizzly bars.

Oversize travels over the bars into the crusher.

video_tutorials.title: Grizzly Feeder — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Grizzly Feeder.
Check for pegged or blocked bar gaps.
Measure bar wear and gap; inspect springs.
Replace grizzly bars and pan liners.
Watch for uneven or reduced feed: feed rate drops, material builds up. Common cause: sticky material.
Watch for cracks in tray or body: visible cracks near stiffeners. Common cause: fatigue from long running at high amplitude.
Watch for pegging/blinding of bars: fines carried to the crusher. Common cause: near-size lumps wedged between bars.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.

questions.question: Why scalp before the primary crusher?
options: To bypass material already smaller than the crusher setting

questions.question: Why are grizzly bars often tapered?
options: To open the gap downwards so near-size pieces do not wedge
